findings.reason: The protected source is already the conventional optimal solution: reject an impossible edge count, then use path-compressed union-find with union by size to reject a cycle. The implementation is concise, exposes both structural tests directly, and meets the required near-linear-time and linear-space bounds, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies paid-only LeetCode problem 261 and its Python execution contract. The Reference preserves the labeled-node and undirected-edge model, and the contract now defines e as edges.length before that symbol is used in the branch complexity bound.

The immutable native source is tied to verified submission 2064285350. It and the app-local source have the same edge-count guard, parent and size initialization, iterative path-halving find, same-root rejection, union-by-size swap, merge update, and final result; only LeetCode wrapper and typing syntax differ.

The legal 32/96/320-node path-tree tiers force all successful unions and were recalibrated so the intended slower control completes rather than hitting the safety cap. The current source passes every workload at +0.04 relative exponent and 1.04x largest ratio; a correct path-search-before-each-insertion control passes all outputs but fails scaling at +1.11 and 122.77x.

The Approach matches the protected source exactly: the n - 1 edge prerequisite reduces validation to cycle detection, successful unions prove connectivity, and the refined complexity explanation accounts for path compression, union by size, and the accepted edge-count relation.

The hash-bound paid-only Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving both factual examples in order, all six constraints, the absence of example explanations and source-native extra sections, and the zero-visual structure.

coverage: both source-fidelity-verified examples remain first and in source order as visible samples with exact node counts, edge pairs, and Boolean outputs
one isolated node covers the exact minimum n and zero-edge boundaries, while connected and disconnected two-node graphs cover the smallest nontrivial tree decision
an acyclic two-component forest distinguishes connectivity from cycle absence and replaces the former hidden disconnected row with visible evidence

n = 2000 with endpoint 1999 covers the inclusive maximum node count and label boundary while remaining a compact disconnected correctness input
all nine expectations matched both an independent edge-count-plus-connectivity oracle and an independent parent-aware cycle-and-connectivity traversal
20,000 seeded random legal simple graphs through twelve nodes matched both independent oracles and the protected current source
the protected current source passed all nine correctness rows and all three unchanged benchmark tiers through the real-test engine; benchmark outputs and runtime scaling passed
all nine correctness rows are visible samples or trials, while the unchanged 32, 96, and 320-node path workloads remain hidden performance-only benchmarks
